claimed_purpose.text: Local-first MCP middleware providing persistent memory, proactive goal enforcement, and autonomous intelligence for AI agents
Provides a knowledge graph memory system for persistent storage of entities, relations, and observations
Storage interface for loading and saving knowledge graphs as the persistence unit
Enables persistent memory across sessions for AI assistants

mechanisms.text: Vector index (entity_embeddings) participates in entity lookup during create_entities; a deleted graph node may persist as a 'ghost' in the vector index and be returned by vector search, causing the crash on merge.

Memory operations are delegated to a KnowledgeGraphManager instance, which is passed into the server and forwarded to the call-tool handler — suggesting a graph-structured store rather than a flat log.
Session continuity via auto-checkpoints every 25 tool calls saving full L1 working memory snapshot, with auto-resume restoring goals and context from the previous session
Proactive memory injection: relevant memories are injected into every tool call by default, configurable via MEMENTO_PROACTIVE_INJECT and MEMENTO_PROACTIVE_TOP_K
Three memory decay rates by type: semantic (~200d half-life), episodic (~50d half-life), working (~14d half-life), each with configurable decay lambda
Delete path covers entities (with their relations), individual observations, and individual relations — supporting partial or full forgetting
Debug tooling bypasses application abstractions to query the Neo4j database directly for entity embeddings, revealing the underlying store
Write path — createEntities merges observations when an entity already exists (deduplication via Set), rather than replacing or erroring
Adaptive retrieve policy: system chooses between vector-only, keyword-only, or hybrid search based on query characteristics
Vector embeddings are stored per entity and synced to a separate VectorStore; on entity delete the vector is also removed
Retrieve fallback: if vector search fails or yields insufficient results, system falls back to text-based keyword search
Scaffold: system prompt instructs the LLM to check the knowledge graph and use semantic_search when answering questions
Vector search uses Neo4j's db.index.vector.queryNodes procedure; retrieve returns ranked entities by score
Non-destructive versioning: updates create new versions rather than overwriting, preserving full history
Entity creation: new entity nodes written to the knowledge graph with name, type, and observations
Full database reset is possible by deleting the data directory and reinitializing the schema
Memento MCP uses Neo4j as a storage backend, accessed via a Neo4jStorageProvider component
Retrieve — full graph read: the entire knowledge graph can be read into context at once
File-based storage is explicitly deprecated in favour of a StorageProvider abstraction
Store backend: Neo4j used as unified storage for both graph data and vector search
Confidence decay on relations is time-based, computed from a half-life parameter
Embedding generation can be forced for a specific entity via a debug tool
Persistence backend: Neo4j graph database with integrated vector index
Embeddings are generated via OpenAI API with a configurable model

ledger.claim: Memento MCP stores a curated knowledge graph (entities + observations + relations) in Neo4j, not a raw message log
ledger.quote: Entities are the primary nodes in the knowledge graph. Each entity has: A unique name (identifier), An entity type (e.g., "person", "organization", "event"), A list of observations, Vector embeddings (for semantic search), Complete version history
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Persistence is in Neo4j; data survives container restarts via Docker volume mounts
ledger.quote: Neo4j data persists across container restarts and even version upgrades due to the Docker volume configuration
ledger.locator: README.md, Storage Backend > Data Persistence and Management section
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Write path supports create, add observations, update, and delete for both entities and relations
ledger.quote: create_entities ... add_observations ... delete_entities ... delete_observations ... create_relations ... update_relation ... delete_relations
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Temporal versioning is non-destructive: updates append new versions with timestamps rather than overwriting

ledger.claim: Relation confidence decays over time with a default 30-day half-life and can be reinforced by new observations
ledger.quote: Configurable Half-Life: Define how quickly information becomes less certain (default: 30 days) ... Reinforcement Learning: Relations regain confidence when reinforced by new observations
ledger.locator: README.md, Advanced Features > Confidence Decay section
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval uses OpenAI embeddings (default: text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) with cosine similarity at a default 0.6 threshold
ledger.quote: Optimized Defaults: Tuned parameters for balance between precision and recall (0.6 similarity threshold, hybrid search enabled)
ledger.locator: README.md, Advanced Features > Semantic Search section

ledger.claim: Retrieve is performed via vector similarity search (cosine or euclidean) against an indexed embedding store, returning ranked entities
ledger.quote:
CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes(
'entity_embeddings', // Index name
$limit, // Number of results to return
$embedding // Query vector
)
YIELD node, score
RETURN node.name AS name, node.entityType AS entityType, score
ORDER BY score DESC
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: When vector search fails, the system falls back to text-based search rather than returning nothing

ledger.claim: A ghost entity can survive in the vector index after its graph node is deleted, and create_entities may resolve that ghost during upsert lookup, triggering the null observations crash.

ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: add_observations receives the observations parameter as a JSON-encoded string rather than a native array, indicating an MCP tool-layer serialization bug in version 0.3.9.
ledger.quote:
"observations": "[\"Test observation...\"]"  // String, not array!
This suggests the MCP tool layer is serializing array parameters as JSON strings instead of passing them as native arrays.
ledger.locator: The Technical Issue / MCP Parameter Serialization Bug
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Dropping and recreating the entity_embeddings vector index did not resolve the create_entities crash, ruling out index corruption as the sole cause.
ledger.quote:
Dropped and recreated entity_embeddings vector index
Result: All failed. The bug is in memento-mcp's server-side code.
ledger.locator: Complete Troubleshooting Log / Vector Index Attempts
